title: Oracle Database Small Examples
description: Use these small Oracle Database examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Ask DUAL for a calculation
examples.description: DUAL is a small built-in table used when a query needs no real table data.
examples.output: The answer is one row with total_books equal to 5.

examples.title: Choose number and text types
examples.description: Oracle types describe the values a column or expression holds.
examples.code: SELECT CAST(12 AS NUMBER(3)) AS pages, CAST('Moon Trip' AS VARCHAR2(40)) AS title FROM dual;
examples.output: The row contains the number 12 and text Moon Trip.

examples.title: Build a small query-only list
examples.description: A WITH query gives a temporary name to a result used by that statement.
examples.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',60 FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'Tiny Seed',20 FROM dual)
SELECT title,pages FROM books ORDER BY pages;
examples.output: Tiny Seed appears before Moon Trip in page-count order.

examples.title: Fetch the first sorted row
examples.description: FETCH FIRST limits rows after the chosen order.
examples.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',60 FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'Tiny Seed',20 FROM dual)
SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY pages,title FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY;

examples.title: Write an unambiguous date
examples.description: A DATE literal names a calendar date in a fixed form.
examples.code: SELECT TO_CHAR(DATE '2026-11-16','YYYY-MM-DD') AS club_day FROM dual;

examples.title: Handle a missing value
examples.description: NULL means a value is missing or unknown.
examples.code: SELECT NVL(CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR2(20)),'Not chosen') AS book_choice FROM dual;

examples.title: Join a book and its author
examples.description: A join combines records whose key values match.
examples.code:
WITH authors(id,name) AS (SELECT 1,'Mia' FROM dual), books(title,author_id) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',1 FROM dual)
SELECT b.title,a.name FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id=b.author_id;
examples.output: Moon Trip is paired with Mia.

examples.title: Count a category
examples.description: GROUP BY makes one result per category. COUNT counts rows belonging to that category.
examples.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (SELECT 'story' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'story' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'science' FROM dual)
SELECT kind,COUNT(*) AS total FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;
examples.output: Science has 1 row and story has 2.

examples.title: Create an identity key
examples.description: An identity column lets Oracle create a numeric id.
examples.output: The new practice table contains a generated id and the title Moon Trip.

examples.title: Read a sequence value
examples.description: A sequence is a separate object that gives out numbers.
examples.code:
CREATE SEQUENCE cma_book_numbers START WITH 100 INCREMENT BY 1;
SELECT cma_book_numbers.NEXTVAL AS number_value FROM dual;
examples.output: The first NEXTVAL is 100 in this newly created sequence.

examples.title: Run a small PL/SQL block
examples.description: PL/SQL adds variables and step-by-step instructions to Oracle SQL.
examples.output: With DBMS Output enabled in the client, the block prints Books: 3.

examples.title: Undo uncommitted sample changes
examples.description: A savepoint marks a point inside a transaction.
examples.output: The extra sample title is not returned after the rollback to the savepoint.
